programs.qualification: DUAL AWARD, both non-official: (1) 'Máster de Formación Permanente' of 25 ECTS accredited by UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, a private university) — i.e. a TÍTULO PROPIO, plus a 'Máster Profesional' route for those without a degree; and (2) a Professional Diploma from SAE Creative Media Education.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. This is a Máster de Formación Permanente / título propio issued under UDIMA's own authority. It is NOT a 'Máster Universitario Oficial', it is NOT ANECA-verified, it does not confer EHEA official master status and it does not give access to a Spanish PhD. NOTE THE ECTS: 25 ECTS is very small — an official Spanish master is 60–120 ECTS. Calling a 25-ECTS course a 'máster' is legal in Spain for a título propio but it is exactly the marketing trap to be sceptical about. Separately, SAE Barcelona's UNDERGRADUATE Título de Grado en Música (240 ECTS, four specialities including Composición de Música Electrónica) IS official — authorised by the Generalitat de Catalunya and validated by AQU Catalunya — but that is a bachelor-level award and is a different thing entirely from this master.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED / LIKELY PROBLEMATIC AS SOLD. SAE Spain publishes an international-students section that explicitly covers 'student visa' guidance for non-EU applicants, and states international applicants need a student visa. However a 25-ECTS, 8-month, non-official título propio is a weak basis for a Spanish student visa, which normally expects a full-time programme of substantial duration at a recognised centre. He must get written confirmation from SAE that THIS specific programme generates a visa-supporting acceptance letter before paying anything.
programs.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, synthesis, live electronics, DJ-adjacent performance, mixing and mastering — the closest published match in Spain to this candidate's stated goal.
programs.whatYouStudy: First semester: sound theory, music theory, MIDI protocol, audio processing, synthesizers, sampling, and mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X. Second semester: advanced production, hardware synthesizers (Moog, Prophet/Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai), sound design, live performance, mastering, and industry career management. Includes the official Ableton Live Production Certificate.
programs.durationEcts: 8 months full-time; 25 ECTS.
programs.language: Spanish. SAE states Spanish-language proficiency is required for international students — a real obstacle for a Tunisian applicant with no Spanish.
programs.intakes: Two intakes per year. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026. Barcelona: October 2026 and February 2027. (These are the currently published dates; the SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 intake is not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE pattern, confirm new dates.)
programs.entryRequirements: An official university degree (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura or Diplomatura) for the 60-ECTS Formación Permanente route; alternatively at least 2 years of documented professional experience for the 'Máster Profesional' route. Minimum age 18. Spanish-language proficiency. Completion of an admission questionnaire and an access interview.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly. The stated requirement is 'una titulación universitaria oficial (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura o Diplomatura)' with no subject restriction — a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies it directly. No music degree, conservatory training or prior audio experience is demanded. This is the most accessible entry route in the whole slice for his exact profile.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is published as a requirement. Admission is by questionnaire plus an 'entrevista de acceso' (access interview).
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An admission interview only.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required — and no English-language route either. Instruction and admission are in SPANISH, and SAE states Spanish proficiency is required of international students. He would need to reach a working level of Spanish (realistically B1–B2) before October 2027.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — SAE runs continuous admissions with Open House Days that carry enrolment discounts.
programs.deadline: No published hard deadline; rolling admission tied to the February and October start dates. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a 2027 start.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. SAE Spain does not publish the price of this master anywhere on its site. Do not accept a verbal quote — insist on a written fee schedule.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. For scale only, and from third-party listings rather than SAE's own pages: SAE's Audio Engineering Diploma (a different, undergraduate-level product) is quoted at around €8,700, ranging roughly €8,000–€10,000 depending on payment plan; SAE's BA/BSc (Hons) Audio Production is quoted at €14,000–€16,000 depending on plan. Neither figure is the price of this master and neither is officially published.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — enrolment fee, materials fee and exam fees are not published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a formal requirement, but the syllabus is built on Ableton Live and Logic Pro X, so a capable laptop and at minimum an Ableton Live licence should be budgeted. An official Ableton Live Production Certificate is included in the programme.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — SAE publishes no price for this programme. Estimating would be irresponsible.
programs.paymentPlans: SAE España operates a published plan structure: Plan A is a single payment that carries an early-payment discount; Plan C is monthly instalments without the discount. Enrolling during an Open House Day reportedly lets students take monthly instalments at the discounted Plan A price. Exact figures UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: SAE Barcelona publishes an institutional discount schedule, but almost none of it reaches a Tunisian non-EU applicant. Available in principle: Active-student/alumni 40%; family members (siblings/cousins/relatives) 20%; disability ≥33% 30%; large-family status 10%; unemployment/ERTE 10%; excellence (9+ GPA in Spanish bachillerato or in SAE's own first year) 60%. The government routes — MEC scholarships and the Generalitat de Catalunya 2026-2027 non-university grants (income-based €1,700, relocation €2,700, basic €300–350, academic performance €50–125) — are for Spanish/resident students and do NOT apply to a newly arrived non-EU student. The Yamaha Europe Foundation grant (€1,000–€2,000, musicians under 25 at recognised European institutions) is the one realistically open award. Net realistic scholarship for this candidate: close to zero, other than possibly the Yamaha grant.
programs.facilities: Barcelona campus: 2,700 m², seven professional audio studios, a production studio with an ICON D-CONTROL digital console, three post-production suites with colour correction, MIDAS F-16 analogue routing stations, MIDI stations with analogue and digital synthesizers, and a cinema mixing suite with 7.1 JBL monitoring and surround panner. Madrid campus: Solid State Logic 4000G+ console and a RAVEN MTX II Slate Digital console (SAE claims to be the only school in Europe with it). Official certification partners: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Cubase, Ableton Live, Wwise, Autodesk, Adobe.
programs.reputationSignals: SAE is a large, long-established international audio-school chain with genuinely serious studio infrastructure — the equipment list is among the best in this slice. Positive signal: SAE Barcelona's undergraduate degree is officially recognised by the Generalitat and AQU, which shows the institution can meet Spanish quality standards. RED FLAGS: no published price for the master anywhere; a 25-ECTS award marketed as a 'máster'; the UDIMA título propio branding is easy to mistake for an official university degree; and a heavy discount architecture that is essentially inaccessible to non-EU students.
programs.recommendation: The best CRAFT fit in Spain for his stated goal — this is literally an electronic-music-production master taught on Ableton and hardware synths, with no music degree required and his software-engineering BSc accepted outright. But three things make me cautious. First, it is a 25-ECTS título propio, not an official master: he must not be sold it as a Spanish degree. Second, the price is not published anywhere, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is a serious governance problem — get it in writing before engaging. Third, it is taught in SPANISH and he has none, so he would need a year of language work before October 2027. My verdict: pursue it as a strong second option behind Berklee, but treat the unpublished fee and the visa question as blockers to clear in writing first.

programs.program: Máster en Producción de Audio
programs.institution: SAE Institute Spain (SAE Creative Media Education)
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio academy — international chain (SAE Institute)
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO. Two routes: a 'Máster de Formación Permanente' of 60 ECTS accredited by UDIMA (requires a university degree), or a 'Máster Profesional' route for applicants with 2+ years of professional experience; plus a Professional Diploma from SAE Creative Media Education.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. Accredited by UDIMA, a private university, as its own título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente — NOT a 'Máster Universitario Oficial', not ANECA-verified, no PhD access. At 60 ECTS it is at least the right size for a master-level award, unlike SAE's 25-ECTS electronic-music master, but the legal status is the same: it is a school/private-university diploma, not an official Spanish degree.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLE BUT CONFIRM IN WRITING. SAE explicitly states that a student visa is required for non-EU citizens and runs an international-admissions pathway with visa guidance. A 24-month, 60-ECTS full-time programme at a centre that also holds official Generalitat/AQU recognition for its degree is a far more defensible visa case than the 8-month electronic-music master. Still, because the master itself is a título propio, get written confirmation of visa-supporting enrolment before paying.
programs.focus: Broad audio engineering: recording, mixing, music production, post-production for film and television, sound design for video games, live sound and emerging technologies.
programs.whatYouStudy: SAE's published summary: 'grabación, mezcla, producción musical, postproducción para cine y televisión, diseño sonoro para videojuegos, sonido en directo y nuevas tecnologías'. Delivered on SSL, ICON D-CONTROL and RAVEN MTX II consoles with Pro Tools, Cubase, Ableton and Wwise certification pathways.
programs.durationEcts: 24 months; 60 ECTS on the Formación Permanente route.
programs.language: Spanish. Spanish proficiency is a stated requirement for international students.
programs.intakes: Two intakes per year. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026. Barcelona: October 2026 and February 2027. September/October 2027 not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm.
programs.entryRequirements: University degree (Grado, Licenciatura or equivalent) for the 60-ECTS route, OR at least 2 years of professional experience for the professional route. Age 18+. Spanish proficiency. Student visa for non-EU citizens. Admission questionnaire and access interview.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES. The published requirement is a university degree of any discipline, or professional experience — no music degree, conservatory background or prior audio work is demanded. His BSc Software Engineering qualifies him directly.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published. Admission by questionnaire and interview.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required. Taught and admitted in Spanish — Spanish-language proficiency required instead.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling admissions tied to the February and October starts.
programs.deadline: No published hard deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the 2027 intake.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED — not published by SAE.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. Third-party aggregator listings for SAE's other Spanish programmes give scale only: Audio Engineering Diploma approximately €8,700 (range €8,000–€10,000 by payment plan); BA/BSc (Hons) Audio Production €14,000–€16,000 by plan. Neither is this master's price.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — enrolment, materials and exam fees not published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as mandatory; a laptop and DAW licences should be assumed. Certification pathways (Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Cubase, Ableton Live, Wwise) may carry separate exam fees — amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. No official figure is published; refusing to estimate.
programs.paymentPlans: Plan A single payment with early-payment discount; Plan C monthly instalments without discount; Open House Day enrolment reportedly grants Plan A pricing on monthly instalments. Exact amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: Same SAE Barcelona discount schedule as above — active student/alumni 40%, relatives 20%, disability 30%, large family 10%, unemployment 10%, academic excellence 60%. Essentially all are structured around Spanish residents or existing SAE students. Government MEC and Generalitat grants are not open to a newly arrived non-EU student. Yamaha Europe Foundation €1,000–€2,000 (under 25) is the one plausible award.
programs.facilities: As above — Barcelona 2,700 m² with 7 studios, ICON D-CONTROL, MIDAS F-16, 7.1 cinema mix suite; Madrid with SSL 4000G+ and RAVEN MTX II.
programs.reputationSignals: Large international chain with real studio assets and industry software partnerships. RED FLAG: complete absence of published pricing for a two-year, five-figure commitment; and the UDIMA título propio branding that a non-Spanish applicant can easily misread as an official university master.
programs.recommendation: A solid, broad audio-engineering education with strong facilities and an entry route that accepts his non-music BSc without a portfolio. At 60 ECTS over 24 months it is the more substantial of SAE's two masters and the better visa case. But it is a general audio-engineering qualification, not a DJ/electronic-producer one — it points at studio and post-production work rather than at the career he says he wants. Combined with the unpublished price and the Spanish-language requirement, I would rank it below the Electronic Music Production master for his goals, and below Berklee for career leverage.

programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical Profesional
programs.institution: DJP Music School (in collaboration with UDIMA — Universidad a Distancia de Madrid)
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio/DJ academy — independent private school partnered with a private university
programs.qualification: DJP Music School diploma PLUS a UDIMA-issued qualification of 60 ECTS. DJP describes it as a 'TÍTULO PROPIO' registered in Spain's RUCT (Registro de Universidades, Centros y Títulos).
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. It is a título propio of UDIMA (a private university), not a 'Máster Universitario Oficial'. UDIMA's own page for the associated Máster Profesional en Producción Musical states in terms: 'enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial' — non-regulated teaching with no official character. RUCT registration of the CENTRE does not make the TITLE official; this is precisely the distinction that trips up international applicants. No ANECA verification, no EHEA official master status, no PhD access.
programs.visaEligible: UNLIKELY AS STRUCTURED / UNVERIFIED. The programme runs 9 months in EVENING sessions only, Monday to Thursday 19:00–21:30 — that is a part-time evening schedule, which is a poor basis for a Spanish full-time student visa. DJP's page notes only that international students without a Spanish bank account should contact admissions about payment methods; it makes no visa claim. He must not assume this programme can host a residence permit.
programs.focus: Electronic and contemporary music production, DAW-centred, with live performance and music marketing — genuinely close to the DJ/producer target.
programs.whatYouStudy: Seven modules: (1) DAW Production; (2) Applied Musical Fundamentals; (3) Composition and Songwriting; (4) Synthesis and Sound Design; (5) Live Performance; (6) Mixing and Mastering; (7) Marketing and Music Promotion. Taught on Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper. Includes masterclasses with working producers.
programs.durationEcts: 9 months; 60 ECTS (as issued by UDIMA).
programs.intakes: One intake per year, in September. The published start is 21 September 2026.
programs.entryRequirements: Not explicitly published on the programme page. The linked UDIMA description says the programme targets anyone 'interested in developing music production skills, whether from scratch or from an intermediate level', including musicians, composers, producers, sound engineers and DJs — no formal prerequisites are stated.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — effectively open access. UDIMA's description explicitly welcomes beginners ('ya sea desde cero') and no music degree or prior experience is required. His profile is unambiguously accepted. That accessibility is also the warning sign: an award that anyone can enter carries correspondingly little selection signal.
programs.englishTest: None required. Taught in Spanish — Spanish is the real language barrier here, not English.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling until places fill for the September start.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; enrolment runs up to the September start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €1,200 enrolment + €4,700 tuition = €5,900 total in a single payment; or €1,200 enrolment + 10 monthly payments of €490 = €6,100 total on the instalment plan. (Figures as published for the 21 September 2026 cohort.)
programs.tuitionTotal: €5,900 (single payment) or €6,100 (instalments) for the whole 9-month programme. No separate non-EU rate is published — non-EU students pay the same.
programs.otherFees: The €1,200 'matrícula' (enrolment) is charged on top of tuition and is included in both totals above. No other application, materials or exam fees are published. Whether the €1,200 is refundable is UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: A laptop and a DAW are implied by the syllabus. The school partly offsets this: students receive 50% off Ableton Live Suite and 30–50% off plugins — a real, quantified saving that most competitors do not publish.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €5,900–€6,100 in tuition and enrolment, plus a laptop and DAW licence (Ableton Live Suite at the 50% student rate), plus Madrid living costs. Total first-year outlay realistically €18,000–€22,000 including living expenses. This is one of the cheapest master-branded options in the slice.
programs.paymentPlans: Two published options: single payment (€1,200 + €4,700) or 10 monthly instalments of €490 after the €1,200 enrolment. No interest is mentioned. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount is published. International students without a Spanish bank account are told to contact admissions for alternative payment arrangements — arrange this before committing.
programs.scholarships: None published. No bursary, fee waiver or non-EU award is advertised.
programs.facilities: In-person only at Calle Pilar de Zaragoza 63, Madrid. Access to Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper; a virtual learning platform; exclusive masterclasses with professional producers; and substantial software discounts (50% Ableton Live Suite, 30–50% plugins).
programs.reputationSignals: DJP is an established Madrid DJ/production school that has also launched an internationally-validated HND in music production, which suggests some quality-assurance discipline. The UDIMA partnership gives a paper trail. RED FLAGS: UDIMA itself labels the associated programme 'sin carácter oficial'; the evening-only schedule undermines any visa story; and the ECTS-to-contact-hours ratio (60 ECTS from Mon–Thu 19:00–21:30 over 9 months) looks generous relative to actual teaching time.
programs.recommendation: Cheap, DJ/producer-relevant, and open to exactly his profile — on content-per-euro it is arguably the best value in this slice. But I would not build an immigration plan on it: the evening-only schedule makes it a weak student-visa vehicle, and the qualification is explicitly non-official. My candid verdict: excellent as a skills purchase if he is already legally in Spain, poor as a route INTO Spain. If he wants both craft and residency he should choose a full-time programme instead. Ask admissions, in writing, one question: 'Does enrolment on this programme support a Spanish student visa for a Tunisian national?' — and act on the answer.

programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical
programs.institution: TAI — Escuela Universitaria de Artes (Escuela TAI)
programs.institutionType: Private art school with university-school status (adscrita), Madrid
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — TAI states this explicitly on its own programme page. 60 ECTS.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. TAI labels it 'Título Propio' on the programme page, and no validating university is named for this particular master. It is therefore the school's own diploma: not a Máster Universitario Oficial, not ANECA-verified, no EHEA official status, no PhD access. TAI's broader status as an 'escuela universitaria' is not the same as this title being official — a very common confusion in Spanish private education.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED. TAI does publish an advisory service for international students, priced at €1,190 + 21% VAT for extracomunitario (non-EU) applicants and €990 + 21% VAT for EU applicants — for 'Grado/Máster Universitario'. The existence of a paid non-EU advisory product implies TAI handles international enrolment routinely, but it does not confirm that a TÍTULO PROPIO master supports a residence permit. Note also that the advisory pricing references 'Máster Universitario', which this programme is not. Confirm in writing.
programs.focus: Music production centred on a single real project; sound technician, musician, DJ, composer and self-taught producer profiles are the stated target audience.
programs.whatYouStudy: A highly practical programme built around producing one real project end-to-end. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED from the pages read; TAI describes it as 'muy práctico, centrado en un proyecto real'.
programs.durationEcts: 1 academic year; 60 ECTS.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, in October. Published start: October 2026.
programs.entryRequirements: Aimed at 'técnicos/as de sonido, músicos/as, DJs, compositores/as o productores/as autodidactas' — sound technicians, musicians, DJs, composers and SELF-TAUGHT producers. Familiarity with DAWs and basic recording knowledge is expected. Admission process: request an appointment (+34 91 167 20 62 / admision@taiarts.com), submit documentation, complete an in-person or video interview, receive a written decision, secure the place with a payment, then formalise enrolment.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES in spirit — the programme explicitly names 'productores/as autodidactas' (self-taught producers) as a target profile, so an absence of formal music education is not disqualifying. But 'familiarity with DAWs and basic recording knowledge is expected', so he needs demonstrable hands-on competence by the interview.
programs.portfolioSpec: No formal portfolio specification is published, but the admission interview plus 'documentación requerida' effectively functions as one. Expect to be asked for work.
programs.auditionSpec: An interview — in person or by video — is a mandatory admission step.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required. The programme is taught in Spanish; Spanish proficiency is the operative language requirement.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling, by appointment with the admissions team.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; admission is by appointment until places fill for the October start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
programs.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. TAI does not publish the tuition for this master; every aggregator lists it as 'a consultar'. TAI's own tarifas page shows only international advisory fees, not programme tuition.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. Do not proceed without a written fee schedule.
programs.otherFees: PUBLISHED: an international-student advisory fee of €1,190 + 21% VAT (= €1,439.90) for non-EU applicants, versus €990 + 21% VAT for EU applicants. This is an administrative support charge, not tuition — and it is a real €1,440 that a Tunisian applicant pays and an EU applicant does not. Reserva de plaza, matrícula and materials fees are UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. DAW familiarity is expected on entry, so a laptop and DAW licence should be assumed.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — tuition is not published. The only known certainty is the €1,439.90 non-EU advisory fee on top of whatever tuition is quoted.
programs.paymentPlans: TAI states it offers 'becas y ayudas al estudio' and financing options arranged through its academic orientation team. No specific instalment schedule or interest rate is published.
programs.scholarships: TAI states generically that it offers scholarships and study grants ('TAI ofrece becas y ayudas al estudio') plus financing through the academic orientation team. NO named award, amount, eligibility rule or deadline is published, and nothing is published about non-EU eligibility. Treat as UNVERIFIED — an unquantified 'we offer scholarships' claim is not a scholarship.
programs.facilities: In-person on the Madrid campus at Calle Recoletos. Specific studio and equipment inventory UNVERIFIED from the pages read.
programs.reputationSignals: TAI is a long-established and visible Madrid arts school with a broad performing-arts offer. RED FLAGS: tuition not published anywhere; a €1,440 surcharge applied specifically to non-EU applicants; 'Título Propio' status combined with the name 'Escuela Universitaria', which invites exactly the misreading this candidate must avoid; and an unquantified scholarship claim.
programs.recommendation: Reasonable content fit — it explicitly welcomes self-taught producers and DJs, which describes him. But I cannot recommend committing to a programme whose price is not published while a non-EU-only €1,440 fee IS published. For a budget-sensitive self-payer that asymmetry is a bad sign. Worth a single email to admision@taiarts.com asking for (a) total tuition for a non-EU student, (b) whether the título propio supports a student visa, and (c) the name and amount of any scholarship he could actually receive. If any of the three comes back vague, walk away.

programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical
programs.institution: CEV — Escuela Superior de Comunicación, Imagen y Sonido
programs.institutionType: Private audiovisual and sound school (also delivers regulated vocational Grado Superior programmes)
programs.qualification: A CEV school 'Máster' — a private certificate. No official university validation is published for this programme, and no ECTS figure is given.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL (on the evidence available). CEV does not publish ANECA verification, a validating university, or an ECTS count for this master. Absent any of those, it is the school's own diploma — a título propio in substance. Note that CEV DOES deliver an officially regulated 'Técnico Superior en Sonido para Audiovisuales y Espectáculos' (a Grado Superior vocational qualification), which is official but is a VOCATIONAL, sub-degree award, not a master. Do not let the presence of official vocational programmes at the school imply that this master is official.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED. Nothing about non-EU student visas is published for this programme. A 1,200-hour, one-year, in-person programme is at least structurally full-time, which helps, but confirmation must be obtained in writing.
programs.focus: Music production and composition across artist projects, film, television, video games and theatre.
programs.whatYouStudy: Five modules: (1) Industria y Música Audiovisual — contemporary production methods, distribution channels and work in the music industry, audiovisual production and film scoring; (2) Producción de Proyecto Musical — students independently produce a professional music project with tutor supervision, typically producing an artist or original compositions; (3) Formación Instrumental — practical piano, electric guitar, bass or drums with ensemble work; (4) Grabación Avanzada en Estudio — capture techniques for acoustic and electronic instruments, DAWs, mixing, mastering, sound design software, synthesis and sampling; (5) Lenguaje Musical y Técnicas Creativas — harmony, arrangement and notation.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year, 1,200 hours. No ECTS published.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, in October.
programs.entryRequirements: Not published in detail. The instrumental-training and musical-language modules imply that some musical grounding is expected.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED. No published bar on non-music applicants, but the compulsory 'Formación Instrumental' module (piano, guitar, bass or drums with ensemble playing) and the harmony/notation module mean a candidate with NO musical training would be at a real disadvantage from day one. This is the most conventionally musical of the Madrid private masters.
programs.auditionSpec: None published, though the instrumental module suggests some level check is likely.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required. Taught in Spanish.
programs.deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €7,245 for the programme, per the educaweb listing for the Madrid campus. CEV's own site lists the price as 'consultar con el centro' — so this figure is aggregator-sourced and should be confirmed directly. Academic year of the figure is UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionTotal: €7,245 total for the one-year programme (aggregator-sourced; confirm with CEV). No separate non-EU rate is published.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no application, matriculation, materials or exam fees are published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. The syllabus covers DAWs, sound-design software, synthesis and sampling, so a laptop and DAW licence should be assumed.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €7,245 tuition plus Madrid living costs, plus unpublished fees and equipment — realistically €19,000–€23,000 for a first year including living expenses, but the tuition figure itself needs direct confirmation.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published. Nothing is advertised for non-EU applicants.
programs.facilities: Madrid campus at C/ Gaztambide 65, 28015. Recording studios and professional-grade equipment are referenced in student reviews; a detailed inventory is UNVERIFIED. Teaching staff are described as active industry professionals with company links that bring real case studies into the classroom.
programs.reputationSignals: CEV holds a CUM LAUDE seal (2019) with an average student rating of 4.6/5, with reviews praising the teaching staff and modern facilities. It is a well-established Madrid audiovisual school that also runs officially regulated vocational sound qualifications. RED FLAGS: no published accreditation, no ECTS, no published entry requirements, no published fees on its own site, and no scholarship information.
programs.recommendation: Decent price for 1,200 hours and a credible school, but the fit is wrong for him. The compulsory instrumental and harmony modules make this a musician's production master, and he has no instrumental training. Combined with the absence of any published accreditation, ECTS or fee information on CEV's own site, I would not put this ahead of SAE's electronic-music master or DJP. Consider only if he decides he wants classical grounding alongside production — which is not what he has asked for.

programs.program: Máster en Producción Musical Discográfica e Ingeniería de Sonido (MPD)
programs.institution: CICE — La Escuela Profesional de Nuevas Tecnologías
programs.institutionType: Private technology/creative-industries training school and authorised certification centre
programs.qualification: A CICE school 'Máster' — a private professional certificate, bundled with vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools, Waves Level A). No university validation and no ECTS are published.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. The word 'Oficial' in the programme title refers to OFFICIAL AVID CERTIFICATION — a software-vendor credential — NOT to Spanish academic accreditation. This is an important and easily-missed marketing construction: 'Máster ... - Oficial de AVID' means Avid-official, not ANECA-official. There is no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status and no PhD access. It is a private certificate.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED / DOUBTFUL. Nothing about non-EU student visas is published. CICE also offers this master ONLINE, which would not support a residence permit at all. Do not assume visa eligibility.
programs.focus: Record production and sound engineering: sound capture, audio processors, mixing, mastering, genre-specific mixing approaches, and vendor certification.
programs.whatYouStudy: A 10-module programme covering foundational and advanced topics: capture of acoustic and electronic sound sources, audio processors, mixing techniques, mastering, and genre-specific mixing approaches. Includes preparation for Official Waves Level A Certification.
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED. No duration in months or hours and no ECTS is published on the sources read.
programs.language: Spanish, with 'elementary English competency' listed as an entry requirement.
programs.intakes: UNVERIFIED. Available in-person in Madrid and also online.
programs.entryRequirements: Published prerequisites are technical rather than academic: Mac OS user-level proficiency; basic familiarity with Pro Tools or comparable software; elementary English competency. No degree requirement is stated.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no academic or music prerequisite is published at all. The entry bar is technical familiarity (Mac OS, Pro Tools basics), which a software engineer clears easily. But note this cuts both ways: an award with no degree requirement is not a postgraduate qualification in any meaningful sense.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS. 'Elementary English competency' is stated as a requirement; instruction is in Spanish.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionPerYear: CONFLICTING AND STALE. One aggregator listing gives €4,233 but shows a start date of May 2018, so that figure is clearly out of date. Another reference gives €5,100 for the master including Waves Level A certification but explicitly NOT including the Pro Tools certifications. A general indication is that CICE masters run around €4,500 and courses around €2,000. CICE's own site was not reachable to confirm. Treat all of these as UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — no current, officially published figure exists in the sources read.
programs.otherFees: IMPORTANT: at least one source states the €5,100 price includes Waves Level A certification but does NOT include the Avid Pro Tools certifications — meaning the vendor exams that are the programme's main selling point may be billed separately. Exam-fee amounts UNVERIFIED. Application, enrolment and materials fees UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Mac OS proficiency is an entry requirement, which strongly implies a Mac is expected. Pro Tools familiarity is expected on entry, implying a licence. Neither cost is published.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. Published figures are stale and mutually inconsistent, and the certification exams may be excluded from the headline price.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published; nothing for non-EU applicants.
programs.facilities: Madrid, Calle Maldonado 48, 28006. CICE is an authorised training centre for a wide range of vendor certifications (Avid, Waves). Studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.reputationSignals: CICE is a long-established Madrid technology-training school with genuine authorised-certification status, and forum discussion of its sound programmes is broadly positive on value-for-money and teaching staff. RED FLAGS: the 'Oficial de AVID' naming that reads as academic accreditation but is not; stale and conflicting published prices; certification exams possibly excluded from the fee; and an online delivery option that carries no visa value.
programs.recommendation: This is a vendor-certification bootcamp wearing the word 'máster'. For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials quickly and cheaply it has real utility — but it is not a postgraduate qualification, it will not support a visa, and it points at studio engineering rather than DJing or electronic production. My verdict: not appropriate as his primary route to Spain. Only worth considering as a cheap skills add-on if he is already living there. Insist on a current written price that states explicitly which certification exams are included.

programs.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with Warner Music Spain) — NOT A FULL MASTER
programs.institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV) in collaboration with Warner Music Spain
programs.institutionType: Private university postgraduate school with a major-label industry partner
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO of Universidad Francisco de Vitoria — a 30-ECTS POSTGRADO (postgraduate certificate). THIS IS EXPLICITLY NOT A MASTER: at 30 ECTS and 3 months it is half the size of even a minimal 60-ECTS master and a quarter of a 120-ECTS official one.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. It is a título propio issued by UFV (a private university) — not a Máster Universitario Oficial, not ANECA-verified, no EHEA official status, no PhD access. And it is not sold as a master: UFV correctly calls it a 'Postgrado'. Credit where due — this is more honest naming than several competitors in this slice.
programs.visaEligible: NO / EFFECTIVELY UNUSABLE FOR A VISA. Three months of evening classes (Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00) will not support a Spanish student visa or residence permit for a non-EU national. Spanish student visas for stays over 90 days require substantial full-time study; a 3-month evening certificate does not qualify.
programs.focus: Music production and artistic direction, with direct exposure to Warner Music Spain professionals.
programs.whatYouStudy: Practical training in composition, editing, mixing and artistic direction, with direct collaboration opportunities with Warner Music Spain professionals. Includes Avid Pro Tools official certification at PT101 + PT110 levels and a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence.
programs.durationEcts: 3 months; 30 ECTS. Monday to Friday, 18:00–20:00.
programs.intakes: One published intake: September 2026 – January 2027.
programs.entryRequirements: Prior training or experience in music or sound ('formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido'). Targeted at musicians, composers, producers, sound technicians and audiovisual professionals seeking to professionalise. Places are limited because of the practical, personalised format.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the requirement is 'prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound', not a music degree. A self-taught producer with a credible body of work could qualify, but a candidate with neither training nor experience would not. He would need his portfolio to be genuinely developed first.
programs.portfolioSpec: None formally published, but with limited places and a prior-experience requirement, work will effectively be assessed at admission.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. Admission is via the postgraduate admissions team (+34 91 709 14 24, postgrado@ufv.es), with a named advisor.
programs.englishTest: No IELTS required. Taught in Spanish.
programs.deadline: No published deadline; limited places for the September 2026 start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a September 2027 edition.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €6,100 total for the 3-month programme, broken down as a €960 enrolment deposit plus €5,540 in tuition fees. (Note the components sum to €6,500 as published, so ask UFV to reconcile the arithmetic before paying.)
programs.tuitionTotal: €6,100 total as headlined by UFV for the whole postgrado. No separate non-EU rate is published.
programs.otherFees: €960 enrolment deposit (included in the headline total). No other application, materials or exam fees are published. The Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 certification and the Ableton Live 12 Suite perpetual licence are INCLUDED — a genuine and unusually transparent inclusion worth several hundred euros.
programs.equipmentRequired: A laptop is implied. Crucially, the two big software costs are covered: an Avid Pro Tools official certification (PT101 + PT110) and a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence are both included in the fee. This is the only programme in the slice that bundles a perpetual DAW licence.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €6,100 in fees for three months, plus Madrid living costs for that period (roughly €3,000–€4,500), plus a laptop. Total around €10,000–€12,000 — but with no visa and no master-level qualification at the end.
programs.paymentPlans: A €960 enrolment deposit followed by €5,540 in tuition fees. No instalment schedule, early-bird or referral discount is published.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published for this postgrado, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants.
programs.facilities: In-person at the UFV Madrid campus, with direct collaboration with Warner Music Spain professionals — the strongest named industry partnership in this slice.
programs.reputationSignals: The Warner Music Spain partnership is a real, checkable industry link rather than vague marketing, and the inclusion of Pro Tools certification plus a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence signals a school that expects students to actually work. UFV is an established private university. Honest naming ('Postgrado', not 'Máster'). RED FLAG: the published cost components (€960 + €5,540 = €6,500) do not match the stated €6,100 total — get the real number in writing.
programs.recommendation: The best industry connection in the slice and refreshingly honest about what it is. But it is THREE MONTHS and 30 ECTS — it cannot be his primary plan. It will not get him a visa, it is not a master, and at €6,100 it costs almost as much as a full 9-month master elsewhere. My verdict: not a route to Spain. Genuinely interesting as a later add-on if he is already resident and wants a Warner-adjacent network plus Pro Tools certification. Listed here so he is not tempted by the 'Warner Music' branding into treating it as a degree.

He does hold a bachelor's degree, so he would receive the master's diploma rather than the lesser certificate.
programs.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED. A one-year, 60-ECTS, in-person programme at a UB-attached centre is a structurally reasonable visa case, and UB affiliation helps, but nothing about non-EU student visas is published. Confirm in writing before committing.
programs.focus: Music and sound for entertainment experiences — games, film, VR, immersive audio and live performance. The most technology-forward music master in this slice and the closest to his software-engineering background.
programs.whatYouStudy: Music notation, interactive scripting, recording techniques, film music, IMMERSIVE AUDIO, sound design, mixing and mastering. programs.deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027 (the source page still referenced an October 2023 start, so the listing is dated).

programs.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — no published figure. Refusing to estimate.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no application, enrolment, materials or exam fees published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. The syllabus spans Logic Pro, Pro Tools, Ableton Live, Unity and Unreal — a capable laptop and several licences should be assumed, though Unity and Unreal have free tiers.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — tuition is not published.

programs.reputationSignals: The Universitat de Barcelona affiliation is the strongest institutional signal of any título propio in this slice, and the game-engine/immersive-audio orientation is genuinely distinctive and commercially relevant. It is described as pioneering in Europe for combining music production, new technologies and sound design. RED FLAGS: no published price; the source listing still shows a 2023 start date, so verify the programme is still running; ENTI's own site blocked automated access, so all details here are second-hand and must be confirmed directly.
programs.recommendation: On paper this is the single best INTELLECTUAL fit for him in Spain — a music-and-sound master that explicitly recruits developers, teaches immersive audio and game-engine integration, and would let his software-engineering degree be a differentiator instead of a gap. It carries a UB name, and as a bachelor's holder he gets the full diploma. Two caveats: the price is not published, and the source data is dated enough that he must confirm the programme still runs. My verdict: email ENTI first, before anything else on this list, and ask for the 2027-28 fee and whether it supports a non-EU student visa. If the price is sane, this is a serious contender — though note it leans toward games and screen audio rather than club/DJ culture.

programs.program: Diploma de Producción Musical (2 years) — NOT A MASTER, undergraduate level
programs.institution: Escuela Microfusa
programs.institutionType: Specialist audio and DJ academy, with UK university progression partnerships
programs.qualification: Microfusa's own DIPLOMA — an UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL award, not a master and not a postgraduate qualification. Its function is to feed into Level 6 (third and final year) of a UK BA/BSc (Hons) at Solent University or the University of Winchester.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain. It is a private school diploma with no ANECA verification and no Spanish official status. Its recognised value comes from the UK progression agreements (Solent University, University of Winchester), which are genuine and checkable, but the resulting degree would be a British bachelor's, not a Spanish master. IMPORTANT FOR THIS CANDIDATE: he already holds a BSc, so studying two years towards a route into the final year of ANOTHER bachelor's degree would be a step sideways, not forward.
programs.visaEligible: LIKELY, structurally — this is a two-year, full-time, in-person programme (Monday to Friday, 5–6 hours a day) at an established school, which is the kind of programme Spanish student visas are designed for. Microfusa does not publish visa guidance in the pages read, so UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed.
programs.focus: Music production, DAW craft, songwriting, studio recording, mastering, sound design and music business — with an explicit electronic/contemporary orientation.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: fundamentals of digital creation — DAWs (Ableton Live, Logic Pro), music production, songwriting, production analysis and branding. Year 2: advanced studio techniques, mastering, Pro Tools, sound design and music-business fundamentals.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time, in-person with virtual learning support. Barcelona schedule: mornings 09:00–14:00 or afternoons 15:30–20:30, Monday to Friday. Madrid schedule: mornings 08:30–14:30 or evenings 16:00–20:30. No ECTS published.
programs.language: Spanish (the Madrid page notes that English-language instruction costs extra).
programs.intakes: Autumn start; a published start date of 5 October 2026 appears on the site, with other dates through the year.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachillerato (secondary school diploma) or equivalent recommended; interviews available for applicants with lower qualifications. For the UK university progression route, IELTS 6.0 in speaking and writing is required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — entry is at secondary-school level, so a BSc far exceeds the requirement. No music background needed.
programs.auditionSpec: None; interviews are available for applicants without the recommended qualification.
programs.englishTest: IELTS 6.0 (speaking and writing) is required ONLY if he wants to progress to the UK bachelor's top-up year. Not required for the Microfusa diploma itself.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling. Maximum 24 students per shift; minimum 8 to run the cohort.
programs.deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for an autumn 2027 start.
programs.tuitionPerYear: PER YEAR, and identical in Barcelona and Madrid: €6,375 paying in full (€300 deposit + €6,075, saving €400); €6,776 on domiciled bank instalments (€300 deposit + €1,420 first payment + 8 monthly payments of €632, quoted at 8.6% APR); or €6,897 on non-domiciled instalments (€300 deposit + three payments of €2,199 due 15 September, 15 December and 15 March). Domiciled instalments require a SPANISH BANK ACCOUNT, which a newly-arrived non-EU student will not have on day one.
programs.tuitionTotal: Two years: approximately €12,750 paying in full each year, up to approximately €13,794 on the non-domiciled instalment plan. No separate non-EU rate.
programs.otherFees: €300 reservation deposit, non-refundable after 14 days, charged each year and included in the totals above. English-language instruction costs extra at the Madrid campus (amount UNVERIFIED). Credit-cost note: the domiciled instalment plan carries an 8.6% APR — that is real interest, not a payment convenience.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a hard requirement. The programme runs on Ableton Live, Logic Pro and Pro Tools, so a laptop and licences should be budgeted. Industry partnerships with Steinberg, Ableton, Pioneer DJ and Avid suggest student pricing may be available.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €12,750–€13,794 in tuition across two years, plus laptop and software, plus two years of Barcelona or Madrid living costs (roughly €12,000–€15,000 per year). Realistic total two-year outlay approximately €38,000–€45,000.
programs.paymentPlans: Three clearly published options per year: lump sum €6,375 (saves €400); domiciled 8-instalment plan €6,776 at 8.6% APR requiring a Spanish bank account; non-domiciled 3-payment plan €6,897. This is the most transparent fee publication of any school in this slice — Microfusa deserves credit for it.
programs.scholarships: None published. No bursary, discount or non-EU award is advertised.
programs.facilities: Barcelona at Ronda Guinardó 65, 08024; Madrid campus also operating. Maximum 24 students per shift. Industry partnerships with Steinberg, Ableton, Pioneer DJ and Avid. Faculty described as having 30+ years of experience. Progression agreements with Solent University and University of Winchester.
programs.reputationSignals: Microfusa is one of the longest-established and most respected specialist production/DJ schools in Spain, with real Pioneer DJ and Ableton industry links and genuine UK degree progression routes. Best-in-slice fee transparency. RED FLAG for THIS candidate specifically: it is an undergraduate-level product and would not advance someone who already holds a bachelor's degree.
programs.recommendation: Excellent school, wrong level. The craft content and the Pioneer DJ / Ableton orientation are close to what he wants, and the pricing is honestly published — but he already has a bachelor's degree, and this diploma exists to route students into the final year of a UK bachelor's. Spending two years and roughly €13,000 to end up with a qualification below the one he already holds makes no sense. Note also that the Microfusa 'Máster en Producción Musical' at €4,700 that still circulates on aggregator sites REQUIRES completion of a Microfusa diploma first, and no longer appears anywhere on Microfusa's own current course listings — treat it as discontinued unless the school confirms otherwise in writing.

But worth knowing about for a specific reason: if he wants to build the portfolio that Berklee, ENTI or UFV will demand, €3,225 for 9 months of small-group Ableton production training in Barcelona is a rational investment — far better value than paying five figures for a título propio 'máster' that carries no official standing. programs.program: Máster Universitario en Acústica, Audio y Vibraciones

programs.qualification: UK Master's degree (MA or MSc) awarded by the University of Hertfordshire. NOT a Dutch degree, NOT NVAO-accredited. This is the only thing at a private Dutch audio institution that is genuinely a master.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO. The award is a UK degree 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire' (site footer, 2025/6 programmes). SAE Institute Netherlands itself is only registered with CRKBO (Centraal Register Kort Beroepsonderwijs = short vocational education register) — CRKBO is a VAT/quality register for short vocational training, it is NOT a degree accreditation and confers no Dutch higher-education status. In practice: a UK-recognised master's degree, valid in the EHEA via the UK award, but with zero Dutch legal status. Institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private, unfunded).
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — specialist audio/creative-media academy (SAE operates ~50 campuses worldwide)
programs.focus: Self-directed, project-based professional practice master. Student develops one major creative project in a chosen specialism; Audio Production is one of the available specialisms (others: Music Business, Film, Game Art, Games Programming, VFX, Web Dev, Content Creation).
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. ECTS value UNVERIFIED (UK master's, normally 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS).
programs.entryRequirements: Three routes: (1) Bachelor degree with Honours at 2:2 or higher in a RELEVANT field PLUS 1 year work experience; (2) at least five years of professional creative-industry experience; (3) completion of SAE's PGCert Professional Development. SAE states the programme accepts applicants without a media-specific degree.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — SAE states applicants without a media-specific degree are accepted, but the published route reads 'Bachelor degree with Honours (2:2 or higher) in a relevant field, plus 1 year's work experience'. A BSc Software Engineering could plausibly be argued as relevant for games/audio programming, but the candidate has NO professional audio experience and NO work experience, so he fails the '+1 year work experience' element and the 5-year-experience route. Route 3 (SAE's own PGCert Professional Development) is the realistic entry — that is an extra paid course. Confirm directly with SAE.
programs.englishTest: IELTS accepted. Postgraduate: IELTS 6.5 overall with minimum 5.5 in each band. Alternatives listed: TOEFL 79, Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 / C2 180, Duolingo 120, PTE, LanguageCert. He has NOT taken IELTS — this must be booked well before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED on the published pages. The programme is project-based, so a project proposal is likely required; confirm with admissions.
programs.auditionSpec: None published (UNVERIFIED — likely an admissions interview given the self-directed format).
programs.whatYouStudy: No fixed taught curriculum. Student negotiates a personal learning contract and produces a major self-directed creative/professional project in Audio Production, supported by weekly webinars, supervisor meetings and virtual conferences. This is a reflective/professional-practice master, NOT a hands-on studio craft course.
programs.facilities: NONE — the programme is fully online. No studio access, no console time, no Atmos room, no live-electronics lab. SAE Amsterdam's physical facilities (Audient consoles, Pro Tools, Ableton rigs, recording studios) belong to the on-campus diploma/degree programmes, not this master.

programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately £6,750 (~€7,900 at typical rates) tuition for the whole programme, plus possible €500 registration, plus his own computer/DAW/licences and IELTS fee. This is by far the cheapest 'master' in this slice — because it is online and delivers no studio time. Living costs are NOT incurred since there is no relocation.
programs.visaEligible: NO. Two independent reasons: (1) the programme is fully online, so there is nothing to relocate for; (2) SAE Institute Netherlands states in writing on its entry-requirements page: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO', and on its course pages: 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands.' Only an IND-recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit, and SAE Amsterdam does not do this.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: SAE is the largest audio-education chain in the world (founded 1976, ~50 campuses), the Amsterdam campus has real professional studios with Audient consoles and Pro Tools/Ableton, and degrees are quality-assured by a real UK university (University of Hertfordshire; Middlesex University for pre-2022 enrolments). RED FLAGS: (a) the awarding partner changed from Middlesex to Hertfordshire in 2022 — validation partnerships at SAE are not permanent; (b) the 'master' has no studio component whatsoever despite being marketed by a studio school; (c) SAE Amsterdam's inability to sponsor a visa is disclosed only in the small print of the entry-requirements page; (d) prices for on-campus programmes are very high relative to Dutch public alternatives (Quora threads flag exactly this). Notable alumni/staff for the Amsterdam campus: UNVERIFIED — the site publishes testimonials rather than named industry staff. Graduate employment outcomes: UNVERIFIED (no published stats).
programs.recommendation: DO NOT ENROL for his stated goal. He wants to become an international DJ/producer and wants hands-on craft — this master delivers zero studio hours, zero console time, zero live electronics, and no relocation to a scene. It is a reflective professional-practice wrapper designed for people who ALREADY have a creative career. He has none, and on paper he does not even meet the entry route (bachelor in a relevant field PLUS one year's work experience). It also cannot support a Dutch residence permit, so it does not get him to Amsterdam. The only scenario where it makes sense is years from now, once he already works in audio and wants a formal master's title cheaply. Skip for September 2027.

programs.program: Advanced Diploma in Music Production & Sound Engineering — Full-time (1 year)
programs.institution: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam (ARI Education NL — franchise of Abbey Road Studios, London / Universal Music)
programs.city: Amsterdam (Atlantisplein 1, 1093 NE — inside the Q-Factory music-makers centre)
programs.qualification: Advanced Diploma — the institute's OWN qualification. NOT a master, NOT a bachelor, NOT NVAO-accredited, NOT awarded by any university. The institute states plainly: 'the Advanced Diploma is not a 3 year degree programme'.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. The only registration published is CRKBO — the institute states it 'is registered as short vocational education (CRKBO) in the Netherlands'. CRKBO is a VAT-exemption and quality register for short vocational training; it is NOT higher-education accreditation and gives the diploma no legal status as a Dutch degree. Institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private/unfunded) — explicitly not eligible for Dutch student loans.
programs.institutionType: International chain campus / specialist audio academy — franchise of the Abbey Road Institute network under Abbey Road Studios (Universal Music Group)
programs.focus: Intensive hands-on music production and sound engineering: studio recording, production technique, mixing, artist relations, industry practice.
programs.durationEcts: 12 months full-time, 48 weeks of tuition. NO ECTS — not a credit-bearing higher-education programme. Timetable: Mon–Thu 10:00–14:00 classroom; Fri workshops; flexible practical studio access Mon–Sat; expected 40 hrs/week total including 20 hrs self-study.
programs.entryRequirements: Music portfolio of 4–8 productions (MP3/WAV) demonstrating different roles (performer, producer, engineer, writer) with your role clearly described per track; academic qualifications documentation; music qualifications OR a motivation letter detailing music knowledge and experience; motivation letter; CV; copy of photographic passport; €200 application fee. No minimum age and no specific prior education is mandated — 'applicants from diverse backgrounds and experience levels' are welcomed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree is required. Published wording accepts 'music qualifications OR a motivation letter detailing your music knowledge and experience level', and no prior education qualifications are mandated. HOWEVER the 4–8 track portfolio is a HARD requirement and he does not yet have it. This is the single most demanding portfolio requirement in this slice.
programs.englishTest: 'Demonstrated competence in English (for non-English speaking countries)'. No IELTS band published — UNVERIFIED whether a formal test score is required or whether an interview suffices. Worth asking, as it could save him the IELTS fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT published requirement: 4 to 8 productions in MP3 or WAV format, which must 'demonstrate different roles, such as performer, producer, engineer, writer', with the applicant clearly describing their specific role in each track. This is the requirement to start building now if he pursues Abbey Road anywhere in the network.
programs.auditionSpec: No formal audition or interview is explicitly required. Applicants unsure of eligibility are invited to contact the institute.
programs.whatYouStudy: Hands-on, industry-developed curriculum in music production and sound engineering delivered in bespoke studio spaces with integrated classrooms. Named module list is NOT published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; request the full syllabus.
programs.facilities: Bespoke studio spaces with integrated classrooms inside Q-Factory, described as 'top-of-the-range, industry-standard equipment in professional studios'. Flexible practical studio access Monday to Saturday — this is unusually generous and is the programme's main selling point. Detailed console/monitor/outboard inventory and any Dolby Atmos room: UNVERIFIED — demand a written kit list.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — no compulsory laptop, software licence or hardware purchase is published. Confirm before budgeting.
programs.intakes: One full-time intake per year, starting October (not September). Published: 5 October 2026. A comparable October 2027 start is expected — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — applications appear to be rolling until the deadline.
programs.deadline: 5 September 2026 for the 5 October 2026 intake — i.e. roughly one month before start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the 2027 intake; expect an early-September 2027 deadline.
programs.tuitionPerYear: The 1-year full-time programme total IS the annual fee. €18,860 (upfront) to €20,160 (monthly plan). Same for EU and non-EU — no differential published. Fees quoted are current on the institute's fees page.
programs.tuitionTotal: Three published plans, whole programme: PLAN A monthly — €20,160 (12 × €1,680); PLAN B per term — €19,380 (3 × €6,460, terms of 16 weeks); PLAN C upfront — €18,860 single payment. Paying monthly costs €1,300 more than paying upfront.
programs.otherFees: €200 application fee — REFUNDED if the applicant does not complete the admission process successfully. No enrolment/matriculation fee, materials fee, exam fee, insurance or comprehensive/services fee is published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist. Payment to ARI Education NL, IBAN NL12 RABO 0158 1674 57, BIC RABONL2U.
programs.paymentPlans: Three plans as above (monthly / termly / upfront). NO early-bird, alumni, referral or sibling discount is published. The only 'discount' available is the €1,300 saving from paying upfront.
programs.scholarships: NONE published — no scholarship, bursary or fee waiver of any kind for non-EU or Tunisian applicants. Not eligible for Dutch undergraduate student loans (the institute states the course is 'not eligible for any kind of student loan' as it is not a 3-year degree). The only financial relief mentioned is a Dutch INCOME TAX deduction on study costs — which requires Dutch taxable income and explicitly 'does not apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed', so it is worthless to a new international student. The institute also warns the rules changed in 2022 and it cannot guarantee eligibility.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €19,060–€20,360 for the year (tuition + €200 application fee), plus Amsterdam living costs of roughly €14,000–€18,000, plus flights. Realistic first-year outlay if attendance were possible: €33,000–€39,000 — for a non-accredited private diploma.
programs.visaEligible: NO — explicitly and in writing. The institute's FAQ states: 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands.' Elsewhere: 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan.' It adds that applicants may still study there 'if you have a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university.' Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is NOT an IND recognised sponsor and cannot host a student residence permit. For a Tunisian national with no other Dutch residence route, this programme is unreachable.
programs.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: the Abbey Road brand is the strongest in the industry; genuine link to Abbey Road Studios London and to Universal Music; located inside Q-Factory, a real working music hub; industry-practitioner teaching staff; unusually generous six-day-a-week studio access; a real portfolio-based selection process, which means cohorts are self-selecting and serious. RED FLAGS: (a) NOT NVAO-accredited and NOT a degree — you pay near-degree money for a private certificate; (b) cannot sponsor a visa, and this is buried in an FAQ rather than stated on the fees or course pages; (c) no named teaching staff, no named alumni and no graduate-employment statistics published anywhere on the site; (d) no accreditation statement at all on the course or home pages; (e) the only 'funding' offered is a Dutch tax deduction that by the institute's own admission does not apply to people who are not yet employed — that is close to misleading for the international audience the page addresses; (f) the fee pages have a history of being out of date (a €16,400 figure from a 2022 update was still circulating). No formal published complaints or regulatory actions were found.
programs.recommendation: OUTSTANDING SCHOOL, WRONG COUNTRY, AND NOT A MASTER. On craft, this is the best hands-on music production and sound engineering training in this entire Dutch slice — real studios, six days a week, Abbey Road pedigree, and a portfolio-selected cohort. But three things kill it for him: it CANNOT get him a Dutch residence permit (stated in writing), it is NOT a master or any accredited degree, and at €19,000–€20,400 tuition plus roughly €16,000 living costs it is one of the most expensive options here for the least formal recognition. He also does not currently have the required 4–8 track portfolio. MY ADVICE: do not apply to Amsterdam. If the Abbey Road brand appeals to him, look at Abbey Road Institute campuses in countries where a private school CAN sponsor a student visa — but even then, understand he would be buying training, not a qualification. The portfolio spec (4–8 tracks showing different roles) is worth adopting as his personal build target regardless of where he applies.

programs.program: MARKET-LEVEL FINDING — no private NVAO-accredited master in sound design or music production exists in the Netherlands
programs.institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutions and all named specialist audio providers)
programs.qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
programs.accreditationStatus: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

programs.focus: Sound design, music production, electronic music production, audio engineering, recording arts, music technology, film and game audio, immersive audio, DJ and electronic performance.

programs.scholarships: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.
programs.totalCostEstimate: For orientation: private Dutch audio tuition ranges from €699 (SAE one-month DJ Certificate) to €37,580 (SAE BA Audio Production Standard, monthly plan). The mid-market one-year full-time option is Abbey Road Institute at €18,860–€20,160. Amsterdam living costs add roughly €14,000–€18,000 per year on top.
programs.visaEligible: THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — NO. Only an IND recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit on a student's behalf, and the IND study register covers higher professional/university education, senior secondary vocational education (ROCs) and IB schools. NOT ONE private specialist audio provider in the Netherlands is a recognised sponsor. Both of the two credible English-language schools say so themselves, in writing: SAE Institute Netherlands states 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands'; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands' and 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan', adding that applicants may only attend if they already have 'a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university'. CONCLUSION: a Tunisian national CANNOT legally relocate to the Netherlands to study at any private audio school. Verify current status yourself at https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-study (updated monthly).
programs.reputationSignals: The Dutch private audio market is small, expensive and structurally unable to serve non-EU students. The two brands worth respecting on teaching quality — SAE Institute Amsterdam and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam — both disclose their inability to sponsor visas only in fine print (an entry-requirements sub-page and an FAQ respectively) while running international-facing marketing. That is the sector's central red flag. A second recurring red flag is nomenclature: Pro Audio Education titles its diploma 'Master Geluidstechniek' for what it concedes is MBO+/HBO- level work, and 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a music-production master. Neither is a master's degree. A third is opacity: three providers (Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, Music Production Academy) publish no prices at all.
programs.recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

programs.institutionType: Private university (Universidade Católica Portuguesa is a private, State-recognised university established under Concordat; Escola das Artes is its arts faculty in Porto)

Escola das Artes is a registered unit of UCP in the DGES SIMGES register and its Som e Imagem 1st cycle carries DGES registration 2265/9457. The exact A3ES registration number for the MESTRADO is UNVERIFIED — ask admissions for the 'registo A3ES / despacho' reference in writing before paying anything. programs.focus: Sound design for film, theatre/concerts, music production, sound art installations, and game audio, inside a wider sound-and-image school (animation, VFX, new media art).
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Project Production I — Exterior and Studio (12), Sound Production for Video Games (5), Electronic Production (5), Sound Arts and Technologies (5), Research in Sound and Image (3). Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): Project II — Post-Production Sound Design (12), Soundtrack (5), Interdisciplinary Project (5), Interdisciplinary Seminar (3), Tangible Interfaces and Physical Computing (5). Year 2 S1: Portfolio and Showreel (3) + Dissertation/Project/Internship (27). Year 2 S2: Dissertation/Project/Internship (30). Content explicitly covers microphone technique, studio recording and mastering, surround mixing for cinema, live sound, game audio and sound art. programs.language: Portuguese. An English-taught route is UNVERIFIED — confirm directly, this is the single biggest practical risk for a Tunisian applicant with no Portuguese.

This is the ONLY programme in this Portuguese slice that names engineering in its own admission wording, which makes it the best structural fit for a BSc Software Engineering holder. Selection still rests heavily on the portfolio and interview.

UCP Porto's general merit scholarship consists of FULL exemption from tuition up to a maximum of 36 ECTS per semester, plus exemption from registration and enrolment fees. The Escola das Artes also lists the Prémio Caixa Geral de Depósitos. Whether a non-EU first-year entrant can win one on entry (as opposed to after a year of grades) is UNVERIFIED. Portuguese State social scholarships (DGES Ação Social) are generally NOT available to a newly arrived non-EU student. Net effect: assume full self-pay for year 1.
