programs.visaEligible: YES. UCP is a State-recognised private university awarding an official 2nd-cycle degree, which is exactly the category that supports a Portuguese D4 residence visa for study (course longer than 12 months). Acceptance letter from UCP + proof of means + accommodation is the standard file.
programs.reputationSignals: The strongest single signal in private Portuguese sound education: A3ES/DGES-recognised degree, a dedicated Sound Design specialisation (rare), a research-active school (Doutoramento em Ciência e Tecnologia das Artes sits above it), motion-capture and surround facilities, and an Erasmus Mundus programme (Digicréa) hosted in the same school. 45 places across all phases, so it is selective but not tiny. No published complaints or red flags found. Caveat: it is a film/media-arts sound school, not a club-music or DJ school — there is one 'Electronic Production' unit (5 ECTS), not an electronic-music pathway.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €7,080–€7,600 (tuition €6,570 + application €50 + enrolment €460, plus unpublished insurance/materials). Full two-year tuition + fees approx. €13,650–€14,500, EXCLUDING living costs in Porto (budget roughly €800–€1,100/month) and excluding a laptop/DAW.
programs.recommendation: STRONGEST PORTUGUESE OPTION FOR HIM — with one hard caveat. It is the only entry in this slice that is simultaneously (a) a genuine A3ES master's degree, (b) explicitly open to an engineering bachelor, (c) visa-safe, and (d) cheap by Western European private standards (€13,140 for the whole degree is less than one year at most Spanish or Dutch private schools). The caveat is language: it is taught in Portuguese, and he does not speak it. If he is willing to spend the coming year on Portuguese to roughly B2, this is arguably the best value-for-money accredited sound-design master in the four target countries. If he is not, it is unworkable and he should look at ReSound instead. Note also that it will NOT make him a DJ — it will make him a film/game sound designer with strong studio craft. He should treat the DJ ambition as something he builds in parallel, not something this degree delivers.

Neutral/negative: Lusófona is a large-volume private university with an admissions funnel of seven phases per year, which is a commercial-intake pattern rather than a selective one; the group has periodically attracted press scrutiny in Portugal over governance. Its Pós-Graduação em Produção e Tecnologia do Som appears to have been withdrawn (see separate entry), so check programme stability before committing.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €4,400–€5,400 (derived tuition €3,800–€4,565 + matrícula €350 + seguro €50 + candidatura €180 or €460), EXCLUDING living costs in Lisbon (realistically €900–€1,300/month, Lisbon is expensive) and equipment. Full-programme tuition + fees roughly €8,200–€10,000. This is one of the cheapest accredited private master's routes in the whole four-country search — but confirm the instalment count in writing.
programs.recommendation: GOOD VALUE, BUT VERIFY THE TUITION IN WRITING BEFORE GETTING EXCITED. The content is the closest fit to what he actually wants of any A3ES-accredited option — synthesis, sound design, studio practice, music computing, Max/MSP, and an evening timetable that lets him produce and gig during the day, in Lisbon, a genuinely live electronic-music city. The published fee structure implies a total cost far below any Spanish or Dutch private equivalent. Three warnings: (1) the annual tuition is not published as a single number and the two conflicting candidatura fees (€180 vs €460) suggest a fee page that is not carefully maintained — get everything in writing; (2) it is taught in Portuguese; (3) 75% of the admission decision is portfolio and interview, and he currently has no portfolio, so he needs twelve months of serious output before applying. Rank this second behind UCP Porto on prestige, first on price.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Ireland) + Universidade Lusófona (Portugal, PRIVATE) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Lithuania), within the FilmEU European University alliance
programs.city: Lisbon (semester 2; semester 1 Dublin, semester 3 Vilnius, semester 4 at any partner)
programs.country: Portugal (one of three countries; the Portuguese partner is the private Universidade Lusófona)
programs.qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
programs.institutionType: International consortium; the Portuguese leg is a private university (Universidade Lusófona / COFAC). IADT is an Irish public institute; LMTA is a Lithuanian public academy.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL and the highest-quality signal available in this slice. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission (project 101180273) and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona's contribution sits under A3ES, IADT under QQI/Ireland, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement.
programs.focus: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and the audiovisual industries — the most internationally-facing sound master's touching Portugal.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four semesters with structured mobility: Semester 1 at IADT (Ireland); Semester 2 at Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon); Semester 3 at LMTA (Vilnius); Semester 4 master's thesis/project at any partner. Detailed per-semester module lists were not extractable from the pages read — UNVERIFIED; request the full programme handbook from the consortium. The Lisbon semester draws on Lusófona's Atmos/3D audio, multitrack studios and acoustic labs.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, in-person, with compulsory mobility across three countries.
programs.language: English — this is the decisive difference from every other accredited option in Portugal.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Critically, the published wording states: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience' in areas such as sound, music, film or media. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, TWO recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES, and this is the exact clause he must clear. Quote: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience.' A Software Engineering BSc is a 'degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound/music/film/media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Between now and a January-2027 deadline he must manufacture that evidence: released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, an audio software project. Without it, this is a rejection.
programs.portfolioSpec: Exactly specified, unusually clearly: maximum 3 examples of sound or media-related work; a single hyperlink to a portfolio site or a compiled file is acceptable; each piece needs a short reflective paragraph stating his role; total realistic listening/viewing time 10–15 minutes. Note the discipline this demands — three strong pieces, not a dump.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition or performance test published. Selection is on documents, portfolio and references; an interview stage is UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: YES — and this is his action item. IELTS 6.0 minimum with ALL components at 6.0 or above. Equivalents accepted: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, LanguageCert ESOL. Tests must be within 2 years of application. Alternative: completion of an EQF Level 4+ qualification with at least one year taught in English — worth checking whether his SMU MedTech BSc, if English-taught, qualifies him for this waiver, as that would save both the fee and the sitting. He has NOT taken IELTS; on a January 2027 deadline he must book it by roughly October 2027... i.e. autumn 2026, immediately.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €7,500 per year for self-funded students (participation costs), charged as €7,500 at semester 1 and €7,500 at semester 3, per the official consortium site. Non-EU pricing is stated to be IDENTICAL to EU pricing — no partner-country surcharge, which is unusual and favourable.
programs.tuitionTotal: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded). CONFLICT FLAG: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page instead quotes an average of about €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (roughly €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat the consortium figure (resound-ma.eu) as authoritative and get the discrepancy resolved in writing before applying.
programs.otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. Because of the three-country mobility, he should also budget for THREE residence-permit processes (Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania) and inter-country relocation — a real, unpublished cost that could easily add €1,500–€3,000 across the two years. UNVERIFIED as a published figure.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A capable laptop and headphones are a practical necessity for a mobility-based sound programme.
programs.paymentPlans: Self-funded tuition is split into two payments (€7,500 at semester 1, €7,500 at semester 3) rather than four. No instalment, early-bird or alumni discount published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: THE BEST SCHOLARSHIP AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, and it is open to him as a non-EU national. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover FULL tuition (he pays €0) plus a stipend of €1,400 PER MONTH, which is explicitly described as contributing to travel, visa and living allowance. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value. Awarded on merit. Number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places — so it is genuinely competitive, but EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category. This is the single item in this whole Portuguese slice that could make his plan free instead of self-funded.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake round opened in autumn 2025. Expect the round for a September 2027 start to open around October–November 2026 — i.e. within months of now. He should be monitoring resound-ma.eu from October 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The last published deadline was extended to 27 January 2026 for the 2026 entry; applications for 2026 are now closed. Expect a comparable late-January 2027 deadline for September 2027 entry. Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadlines are hard and are NOT extended for late portfolios.
programs.facilities: Lisbon semester: Lusófona's professional multitrack studios, acoustic laboratories, cinema post-production and 3D Atmos room. Dublin: IADT's media production facilities. Vilnius: LMTA. Plus the FilmEU alliance network of artists, producers and researchers across Europe.
programs.visaEligible: YES, and better than a single-country route in one respect: Erasmus Mundus students receive structured institutional support for visas at each partner, and the €1,400/month stipend comfortably satisfies proof-of-means tests. Counterpoint: three separate immigration processes in two years is administratively heavy for a Tunisian passport holder, and Ireland is outside Schengen — factor in Irish immigration (IRP) separately from the Schengen leg.
programs.reputationSignals: European Commission selection and funding; FilmEU European University alliance membership; three national accreditations; capped at 24 students a year (so genuinely small cohorts); explicit English-medium delivery. This is the most prestigious sound qualification reachable through a private Portuguese institution. No red flags found. The only structural caveat is that only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in Lisbon specifically, this scatters him across three countries.
programs.totalCostEstimate: With an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: effectively €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month. Without a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + relocation/permits, i.e. a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years.
programs.recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE — and the only one that is taught in English and can be fully funded. The maths is decisive: an Erasmus Mundus scholarship converts a €30k+ plan into a funded one with a €1,400/month stipend, which for a budget-sensitive Tunisian self-payer is transformative. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work: 24 places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause that requires 'relevant prior experience' he does not yet have. His concrete twelve-month plan should be (1) book IELTS now and clear 6.0 in every band — or verify his BSc's English-medium waiver; (2) build the three portfolio pieces the spec asks for, at 10–15 minutes total, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software/interactive piece that leverages his engineering background as a differentiator rather than a liability; (3) secure two recommenders now; (4) watch for the call opening around October 2026. If he only does one thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and Lusófona's own mestrado as the paid fallbacks.

programs.program: Mestrado em Comunicação Audiovisual e Multimédia
programs.institution: IADE — Faculdade de Design, Tecnologia e Comunicação, Universidade Europeia (Grupo Universidade Europeia; international private group, formerly Laureate, now Ensinus/Global University Systems ownership lineage)
programs.qualification: MESTRADO (2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS) — a real degree.
programs.institutionType: International-chain private university (Universidade Europeia group). IADE is its design/technology/communication faculty.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. A3ES registration R/A-Cr 25/2019/AL03 dated 06/04/2023, Despacho n.º 5028/2023 of 27 April 2023. Fully accredited Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree.
programs.focus: Audiovisual and multimedia communication — NOT a sound programme. Sound design appears only as one of several listed career outcomes.
programs.whatYouStudy: Digital Animation Lab; Living Lab I — Digital Journalism; Audiovisual Projects & New Formats; Web Lab; Living Lab II — Infographics & Information Visualization; Transmedia Project; Artificial Intelligence for Future Scenarios. Students have access to an 'estúdio de som e imagem'. NO dedicated sound-engineering, mixing, mastering or electronic-music modules are published — this is the key disqualifier for his goals.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester).
programs.language: Portuguese. An English option exists for some IADE programmes but is UNVERIFIED for this one.
programs.entryRequirements: Not detailed on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. IADE accepts applications year-round subject to available places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Almost certainly yes — it is a communication/multimedia master with no music prerequisite, and IADE's admissions are open-access in character (rolling applications, no published selective criteria). But this cuts both ways: low barrier signals low selectivity. Exact wording UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is held.
programs.englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Programme is Portuguese-medium so IELTS is unlikely to be the relevant test; Portuguese proficiency would be.
programs.tuitionPerYear: 2026/27 published price list: base €509.30 per month × 11 monthly instalments = €5,602.30 per year. A discounted rate of €458.30/month (10% reduction) is published alongside it, subject to limited places allocated in the master's selection process.
programs.tuitionTotal: €11,204.60 total base tuition for the 2-year master's at the 2026/27 rate (€5,602.30 × 2). With the 10% reduction: €10,082.60. NON-EU NOTE: IADE's 2026/27 price list applies a separate, higher non-EU rate ONLY to 'Creative Computing and Artificial Intelligence' (€592.60/month vs €565.60 base). Comunicação Audiovisual e Multimédia carries NO published non-EU surcharge — he would pay the same €509.30/month as a Portuguese student. The non-EU definition used is: nationals of non-EU countries who, at application, do not legally reside in Portugal or have not resided there continuously for more than two years — which describes him exactly, so confirm in writing that no surcharge is added.
programs.otherFees: 2026/27 emolumentos for Mestrados, published as a table totalling €880: Candidatura (application) €75; Matrícula (registration) €375; Inscrição (enrolment) €400; Seguro Escolar (school insurance) €30. Materials, equipment and exam fees: not itemised — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A design/multimedia school of this type will in practice expect a personal laptop and Adobe Creative Cloud; budget for it.
programs.paymentPlans: Tuition is billed in 11 monthly instalments per year. IMPORTANT CONDITION: payment in 11 instalments and/or the award of any scholarship REQUIRES activation of direct debit (débito direto) — which requires a Portuguese bank account, a real practical hurdle for a newly arrived non-EU student. Discounts published: Early Bird (reduced base annual tuition for first-time registrants who register in advance, amount UNVERIFIED); alumni/final-year 'special conditions' (amount UNVERIFIED, applied for the whole programme duration).
programs.scholarships: MERIT SCHOLARSHIP (Bolsa de Mérito): students with a final bachelor's average of 15.5 or above — or 16.5 or above for students from FOREIGN institutions — receive a 40% reduction on the base tuition fee, renewed annually provided the average is maintained. This is directly usable by him IF his SMU MedTech GPA converts to 16.5+/20 on the Portuguese scale, which is a high bar (roughly a strong first-class equivalent). Applied to this programme, 40% off would bring tuition to about €3,361/year, €6,723 total. IADE's fees page also mentions a 'Merit Students Programme' with reductions up to 50% for averages of 16+, and 'Bolsa Interna' and 'Bolsa de Apoio ao Estudo' categories — the published table's 10% column corresponds to one of these, subject to limited places. Portuguese State DGES social scholarships are listed but are not realistically open to a new non-EU arrival. A 10% discount for international candidates (limited places, first-come order) is referenced in IADE marketing — UNVERIFIED against the official price list.
programs.intakes: Rolling — 'candidatos podem formalizar candidatura ao longo de todo o ano' (applications accepted year-round), subject to available places. Main start is September.
programs.applicationOpens: Open year-round. No fixed opening date.
programs.deadline: No published fixed deadline — applications accepted throughout the year subject to vacancies. For a September 2027 start with a Tunisian visa file, he should still apply by roughly March–April 2027.
programs.facilities: Sound and image studio ('estúdio de som e imagem'), specialised laboratories and studios. No console, monitoring, Atmos or microphone inventory is published for the sound facilities specifically — UNVERIFIED, and notably thinner disclosure than UCP Porto or Lusófona.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Universidade Europeia/IADE is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 2-year degree, which supports a D4 study residence visa. As an international-chain university it has established international admissions machinery.
programs.reputationSignals: Positive: A3ES accredited with a specific registration reference; IADE is a long-established and well-regarded Lisbon design school; transparent published price list (better fee disclosure than most schools in this search); a clear, quantified merit scholarship. Negative for HIS purposes: this is a communication/multimedia degree with essentially no sound curriculum — the audio content is one studio and a career-outcomes bullet. Also note the commercial signals: rolling year-round admissions, a discount architecture with at least four overlapping scholarship categories, and mandatory direct debit to access instalments or scholarships. That is a sales-led model, not a selective one.
programs.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €6,482 (tuition €5,602.30 + emolumentos €880), before laptop/software and Lisbon living costs. Two-year total tuition + fees approx. €12,085 at base rate; approx. €7,600 if he secures the 40% merit scholarship.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — WRONG SUBJECT. The accreditation is genuine, the fees are transparent and the merit scholarship is real and quantified, so it is not a bad institution. But he wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music, and this degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs. Paying €11,200 for a communication master that touches sound once, in a language he does not speak, would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money. Include it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants a Portuguese accredited degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training. If he does pursue it, the 40% merit scholarship at 16.5+/20 is the only thing that makes the price sensible.

programs.program: Curso Técnico de Som — SHORT COURSE, NOT A MASTER'S AND NOT A DEGREE
programs.institution: ETIC — Escola de Tecnologias, Inovação e Criação
programs.qualification: NOT A DEGREE AND NOT A POSTGRADUATE QUALIFICATION. Classified as 'Outra Formação Profissional' (OFP) with 'Certificação Nacional' — a DGERT-certified vocational training certificate. It is not a mestrado, not a pós-graduação, and carries no ECTS.
programs.institutionType: Specialist private audio/creative-media academy (DGERT-certified training entity, not a higher-education institution)
programs.focus: Entry-level studio and live sound technician craft.
programs.whatYouStudy: Five modules: Introduction to Sound (audio fundamentals, physics, perception); DAW Avid Pro Tools; Audio Cable Maintenance (identification, soldering, troubleshooting); Capture, Recording & Mixing (studio technique, microphone placement); Live Sound 1 (PA systems, consoles, event management). Project-based, in Portuguese.
programs.durationEcts: 170 hours over ONE SEMESTER. No ECTS. Classes Monday/Wednesday/Friday 19:00–23:00. Maximum 18 students per cohort.
programs.entryRequirements: Preferably completed 12th grade or proven professional experience; motivation letter setting out objectives; portfolio or showreel; interview (in person or online).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music or audio background required; it is an introductory technician course. His software engineering degree far exceeds the stated 12th-grade minimum. This is the easiest entry of anything in this report.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Portefólio ou showreel' required, plus a motivation letter. No format, length or content specification published — UNVERIFIED. In practice, at this level the portfolio is a screening formality rather than a competitive filter.
programs.auditionSpec: Admission interview, available in person OR ONLINE — which makes it accessible from Tunis without travel.
programs.englishTest: None. Instruction is in Portuguese, so Portuguese is the real language requirement — no IELTS involved.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €2,125 for the single semester (this is the whole course; there is no second year).
programs.tuitionTotal: €2,125 total, 2026 price list. Payable as 6 × €354.17. Upfront ('pronto pagamento') price €2,018.75, which already includes the 5% early-settlement discount. No non-EU differential — the price list explicitly addresses non-residents (see payment plans).
programs.otherFees: Inscrição (enrolment) €180, payable at matriculation and NON-REFUNDABLE except if the course does not open. Total cash outlay therefore €2,305 on the instalment plan or €2,198.75 paying upfront. No separate materials, insurance or exam fees are published — UNVERIFIED. ETIC's published caveat: 'Os preços e condições de pagamento podem sofrer alterações até ao início das inscrições' (prices and payment terms may change up to the opening of enrolments).
programs.equipmentRequired: Nothing mandatory published. ETIC supplies individual Apple iMac workstations running Pro Tools, studios with Universal Audio preamps and Genelec monitors, consoles (Midas, Allen & Heath, Behringer, Yamaha), microphones (Neumann, Sennheiser, AKG, Shure, DPA), mobile production units and instruments. A personal laptop is not stated as required — UNVERIFIED.
programs.paymentPlans: Published in detail: 6 monthly instalments of €354.17, or upfront €2,018.75. DISCOUNTS: pronto pagamento (upfront) 5%; EX-ALUNOS (former students) 6%; PARCERIAS (partner organisations) per established protocols. SPECIFIC NON-RESIDENT CLAUSE: 'Cidadãos sem residência fiscal em território nacional: Pronto pagamento — Desconto de 5%' — citizens without Portuguese tax residence get the 5% upfront-payment discount, i.e. he is explicitly catered for. Bank financing available via Caixa Geral de Depósitos, Santander, Banco CTT and BPI (requires Portuguese banking relationship — a practical barrier for a new arrival).
programs.scholarships: NONE. No scholarship, bursary or fee waiver of any kind is published for this or any ETIC short course — UNVERIFIED but consistent across all ETIC course pages reviewed. The only price reductions are the commercial discounts above.
programs.intakes: Annual intake starting OCTOBER. October 2026 start is published. Some ETIC courses run more than one cohort per year — UNVERIFIED for this one.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Enrolments for the October 2026 cohort are open now. The October 2027 cohort's opening date is not published.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No published application deadline; enrolment runs until the cohort of 18 fills. Places are limited and allocated by enrolment order.
programs.facilities: Genuinely strong for the price: individual iMac/Pro Tools workstations; professional recording studios with Universal Audio and Audient preamps and Genelec monitors; Midas, Allen & Heath, Behringer and Yamaha consoles; RCF line arrays; Neumann/Sennheiser/AKG/Shure/DPA microphone locker; Sound Devices and Tascam portable recorders; mobile production units; guitars, bass and drums. Ableton Live, Logic and Pro Tools all available.
programs.visaEligible: NO — this is the critical point. A 170-hour, single-semester vocational course cannot support a Portuguese D4 study residence visa, which requires a course longer than 12 months. At best it might support a short-stay E9 temporary study visa (90 days to 12 months), and even that is UNVERIFIED for OFP-category training. ETIC publishes nothing about visa sponsorship for non-EU students. He CANNOT relocate to Portugal on this course.
programs.reputationSignals: ETIC is a long-established and well-known Lisbon creative school with a real, well-specified equipment inventory (the most transparent kit list of any school in this slice) and DGERT certification. Small cohorts (18). The honest framing: it is a good vocational school, not a higher-education institution, and it does not pretend otherwise — it correctly labels its courses 'Outra Formação Profissional' rather than dressing them up as masters. No red flags found. Weakness: no published graduate-outcome data, no named notable alumni or staff.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €2,198.75 to €2,305 for the course itself, plus roughly €1,000–€1,300/month of Lisbon living costs for the ~5-month duration (€5,000–€6,500), plus flights. All-in realistically €7,500–€9,000 — for a certificate with no visa route and no academic standing.
programs.recommendation: NOT A MASTER'S — DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH ONE, AND IT CANNOT GET HIM A VISA. That said, it is honest, cheap, extremely well-equipped and pitched exactly at his current level (no audio background needed, online interview, 12th grade minimum). Its real use to him is as PORTFOLIO FUEL, not as a destination: the piece he is missing for UCP, Lusófona and above all ReSound is demonstrable sound work, and €2,125 of hands-on Pro Tools, microphone technique and mixing would produce it. But he could get equivalent portfolio material in Tunisia or online for far less, and the €5,000+ of Lisbon living costs to attend a non-visa-eligible certificate makes no financial sense for a budget-sensitive candidate. Verdict: skip unless he is already in Portugal for another reason.

That final track is exactly the kind of artefact the ReSound portfolio spec asks for. But it is a certificate with no academic standing and no visa eligibility, and paying Lisbon living costs to attend would consume a large chunk of his budget for something that does not advance his degree or immigration position. Treat it as a benchmark for what portfolio-building costs, and look for the equivalent locally or online first.

The RTP-studios setting in Porto is a real asset and the 200-hour hybrid format is sensible. But he is a budget-sensitive non-EU applicant, and this school publishes no price, no payment plan, no equipment list and no curriculum, while flagging that official certification is registered for trainees resident in Portugal. That is three unknowns and one probable exclusion. If he is curious, the only correct next step is to email and demand, in writing: total price, enrolment fee, instalment options, and an explicit statement of what certificate a NON-RESIDENT receives. Until then it is not comparable to ETIC or ProDJ, both of which publish everything.

programs.program: Curso Master Producer (Producer I + Producer II) — SHORT COURSE, NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE DESPITE THE NAME
programs.institution: ProDJ Academy
programs.qualification: NOT A DEGREE AND NOT A MASTER'S. The word 'Master' in 'Master Producer' is a marketing label for an advanced course, NOT an academic master's degree. It is a DGERT-certified vocational diploma with no ECTS and no academic grau. This is exactly the naming trap to watch for.
programs.institutionType: Specialist private DJ and electronic-music-production academy (DGERT-certified training entity, not higher education). Describes itself as the only DGERT-certified DJ and music production academy in Portugal.
programs.focus: Electronic music production and DJing in Ableton Live — by far the closest institutional match in Portugal to his stated goal of becoming an international DJ/producer.
programs.whatYouStudy: Producer I: DAW introduction, MIDI manipulation, beat construction, musical composition (scales, chords, progressions), analogue and digital synthesis, audio engineering fundamentals (compression, EQ, mixing), introduction to mastering. Producer II: advanced production processes, mixing techniques, sound design, vocal treatment, compression variations, sidechain effects, professional mastering. Plus 40 hours of professional studio access bookable online and usable up to 3 months after the course ends, 20 hours of 'LAB' Q&A sessions with instructors, four video tutorials with instructor corrections, and access to online classes from other timetables.
programs.durationEcts: 200 hours over approximately 10 months. No ECTS. Multiple weekly timetable options in both cities.
programs.language: Portuguese — UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists.
programs.entryRequirements: Extraordinarily low: minimum age 14; basic computer literacy; any special health conditions to be documented at registration. No portfolio, no interview, no prior music knowledge.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely. Minimum age 14 and basic computer skills are the only stated requirements. There is no academic prerequisite at all. Be clear-eyed about what that means: this is an open-enrolment commercial course, and the absence of any selection is itself information about what the certificate is worth.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.tuitionPerYear: €2,490 upfront for the full 200-hour Master Producer course (Lisbon and Porto, same price). Alternatives: 4 monthly instalments of €622.50, or from €320/month over 10 months.
programs.tuitionTotal: €2,490 total tuition (upfront price). The 10-month plan 'from €320/month' implies up to €3,200 if taken over ten payments — a materially higher total, so the instalment route costs more. No non-EU differential published.
programs.otherFees: Enrolment/registration fee €420 (stated to vary by payment method). Diploma issuance fee €45 — charged SEPARATELY, i.e. the certificate itself is an extra. Total realistic outlay: €2,955 upfront (€2,490 + €420 + €45) or up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month plan. No insurance or materials fee published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published as mandatory — UNVERIFIED. In practice an Ableton Live licence and a laptop are needed; the course includes 40 hours of studio access, which partly offsets this. Confirm whether an Ableton licence is included or must be purchased.
programs.paymentPlans: Three published options: upfront €2,490; 4 × €622.50; from €320/month over 10 months. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: NONE published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: MULTIPLE intakes per year — several 2026-2027 start dates published for Lisbon (weekend and weekday options) with more limited availability in Porto. This rolling-intake pattern is typical of commercial academies.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — enrol at any time for the next available cohort.
programs.deadline: No deadline; rolling enrolment by cohort start date.
programs.facilities: In-studio learning with professional equipment in both Lisbon and Porto; 40 hours of bookable professional studio time included, usable up to 3 months post-course; 20 hours of LAB mentoring. Detailed equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.visaEligible: NO. Although the 10-month duration is longer than most courses in this slice, it is still under the 12-month threshold for a D4 study residence visa, and vocational OFP training at a non-higher-education academy is not a recognised visa-sponsoring category. ProDJ publishes nothing about visa support for non-EU students. He CANNOT move to Portugal on this.
programs.reputationSignals: Positive and genuinely relevant: DGERT certification (it claims to be the only DGERT-certified DJ/production academy in Portugal), instructors holding CCP pedagogical credentials, two campuses, included studio hours, and a syllabus squarely aimed at electronic music and DJing — which is what he actually wants. Negative: age-14 minimum and no selection whatsoever; the 'Master Producer' name invites exactly the confusion this report exists to prevent; a separate €45 charge to issue the diploma; an enrolment fee (€420–€520) that varies by payment method, which is an odd and slightly opaque practice; and instalment plans that increase the total cost without this being flagged. No independent graduate-outcome data or notable alumni published.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €2,955 all-in paying upfront (tuition €2,490 + enrolment €420 + diploma €45). Up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month instalment plan. Plus living costs if attending in person in Lisbon or Porto (~€900–€1,300/month for 10 months = €9,000–€13,000) — which dwarfs the tuition and is unfunded and visa-less.
programs.recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY. Be direct with him: if the only goal were 'learn to produce electronic music and DJ', this is the most on-target training in Portugal, and €2,955 is not unreasonable for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours. But it is not a master's despite its name, it confers no academic credit, and critically it CANNOT get him a residence permit — so he would be paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status. The rational play is the inverse: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or funded ReSound) to obtain the visa and the residence permit, and then, once legally resident, add a ProDJ or ETIC specialisation as a cheap evening top-up. Never the other way round.

programs.reputationSignals: Positive: genuine international brand with campuses in London, Los Angeles, Barcelona and Lisbon; official Ableton Certified Training Center; EP-as-deliverable structure; one-to-one mentoring; Ableton EDU discount; likely English-medium. The pattern of an international chain advertising a UK degree pathway that is not actually available at the campus being marketed is precisely the kind of marketing framing to be sceptical of.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — cannot be estimated without a quotation. The only anchor is €90/hour private tuition, which is expensive. Demand a written total.
programs.recommendation: TREAT WITH SCEPTICISM AND DO NOT COMMIT WITHOUT A WRITTEN QUOTE. On content and probable language of delivery it is attractive: English-medium electronic music production in Lisbon, with an EP as the output and Ableton certification — arguably closer to 'international DJ/producer' than any accredited degree here. But it publishes no prices, holds no Portuguese accreditation, offers no ECTS, cannot support a visa, and advertises a BA (Hons) pathway that is not delivered at the campus he would attend. For a budget-sensitive applicant, an unpriced, unaccredited certificate from an international chain is the highest-risk item in this report. If he is curious, the correct approach is a written quotation for the 120-hour Electronic Music Producer Program including all fees, plus an explicit written statement of what he receives and whether any UK degree route is available in Lisbon. Expect the answer to the second question to be no.
